This is the simulation from [16](../concepts/sixteen.qmd), written in R. It runs in your browser with [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/), a version of R compiled to WebAssembly, so there is nothing to install. The first time, your browser downloads R itself, which can take a minute. Edit any line and click **Run Code** to try it with other values.

## Power for a main effect and for an interaction

A 2×2 experiment with `n` people in each cell and an outcome with standard deviation 1. The main effect is `theta`. The interaction, a difference of differences, is half as large.

```{webr}
set.seed(80)
theta <- 0.4 # main effect, in standard-deviation units
delta <- theta / 2 # interaction (difference of differences): half of theta

# Cells in the order (a, b) = (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1), coded -1/2 and +1/2
a <- c(0, 1, 0, 1) - 0.5
b <- c(0, 0, 1, 1) - 0.5
mu <- theta * a + delta * a * b # true cell means

power_at <- function(n, n_sims = 2000) {
  # Each row is one simulated study: the four observed cell means
  m <- matrix(rnorm(4 * n_sims, sd = 1 / sqrt(n)), ncol = 4) +
    rep(mu, each = n_sims)
  main <- ((m[, 2] - m[, 1]) + (m[, 4] - m[, 3])) / 2 # se = 1 / sqrt(n)
  inter <- (m[, 4] - m[, 3]) - (m[, 2] - m[, 1]) # se = 2 / sqrt(n)
  c(
    main = mean(abs(main) > 1.96 / sqrt(n)),
    interaction = mean(abs(inter) > 1.96 * 2 / sqrt(n))
  )
}

ns <- c(10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320, 640, 1280)
pw <- sapply(ns, power_at)
colnames(pw) <- ns

matplot(ns, t(pw),
  type = "b", pch = 19, lty = 1, log = "x",
  col = c("#d6604d", "#2166ac"), ylim = c(0, 1),
  xlab = "People per cell (log scale)", ylab = "Power"
)
abline(h = 0.8, lty = 2, col = "grey50")
legend("bottomright", c("Main effect", "Interaction"),
  col = c("#d6604d", "#2166ac"),
  pch = 19, lty = 1, bty = "n"
)
round(pw, 2)
```

## The sample sizes for 80% power

The normal approximation gives the same answer without simulation. The interaction's standard error is twice the main effect's, and the interaction is half as large, so its z-score is a quarter of the main effect's. Matching it takes 4² = 16 times the sample.

```{webr}
z <- qnorm(0.975) + qnorm(0.80)
n_main <- (z * 1 / theta)^2 # people per cell, main effect
n_int <- (z * 2 / delta)^2 # people per cell, interaction
round(c(main_effect = n_main, interaction = n_int, ratio = n_int / n_main), 1)
```
